# BACTEREMIA ASSOCIATED WITH STREPTOCOCCI

Bacteremia is typically caused by S. pyogenes (Group A), S. agalactiae (Group B)

and S. pneumoniae. If other streptococcal species are isolated contamination is

likely. Treat only if greater than one blood culture is positive. Identification

and treatment of the source of infection, in addition to antimicrobial therapy,

is crucial for resolution of infection.

For patients with toxic shock syndrome refer to those recommendations.

[Toxic Shock Syndrome](orzid2-gmenu-toxic-shock-syndrome)

# Duration of treatment

Treatment duration is not well established. Treat for 7 -14 days depending on

source control and response to treatment. Consult ID for more information.

# Treatment of S. pyogenes (Group A), S. agalactiae (Group B) and S. pneumoniae

[Penicillin G 4 million units IV q4h \($$\) R](psjizid-penicillin-g-4-million-units-iv-q4h)

# Treatment of other streptococcal isolates with 2 of 2 blood cultures positive or

# alternative to above

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)
